ns2:section.sectionText: SP25 - ENGL 350 - Writing about Literature, Text, and Culture - African American Literature, the Cold War, and the Universal Man - Christopher Freeburg - African American writing solidified its footing and flourished in the middle of the twentieth century during the Cold War. This course explores how Black writers stretched and reimagined their specific local conditions in Illinois, Mississippi, and New York to incorporate “universal” themes that would attract wider audiences. Black music and entertainment also exploded in rock, jazz, and gospel music. This music shaped Black literary artistry. What is more, this course grapples with this turbulent historical moment where Black writers’ voices were heard, but they still did not have full guaranteed rights and privileges in the US. We’ll read Richard Wright, James Baldwin, Paul Marshall, Gwendolyn Brooks, and William Gardner Smith, paying special attention to debates between literary scholars about the future direction Black writing. There will be two major papers and weekly writing assignments.
